Effect of each design lever on performance

Source: R/plot-tradeoff.R
rh_plot_levers.Rd

From a chosen operating point, applies a multiplicative change to each lever (catchment area, reservoir capacity and demand) one at a time and shows the resulting performance metric, with a dashed line at the baseline, so that enlarging the roof, enlarging the tank and trimming demand can be compared directly.

Usage

rh_plot_levers(
  precip,
  base,
  changes = list(area = 1.25, capacity = 1.25, demand = 0.9),
  metric = "attendance_pct",
  dates = NULL,
  climatology = FALSE
)

Arguments

precip

Numeric vector of daily precipitation (mm). If climatology = TRUE, it is first collapsed to its day-of-year mean (see dates).

base

Named list with the operating point (must include the levers to be changed, e.g. area, capacity, demand).

changes

Named list of multiplicative factors applied to each lever in turn, e.g. list(area = 1.25, capacity = 1.25, demand = 0.9).

metric

Single metric to compare (default "attendance_pct").

dates

Optional date vector aligned with precip, required only when climatology = TRUE.

climatology

If TRUE, simulate on the day-of-year climatology (much faster) instead of the full series. Default FALSE.

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  rh_plot_levers(
    precip_pi$value,
    base = list(demand = 6.6, area = 4170, capacity = 400,
                runoff = 0.85, efficiency = 1),
    dates = precip_pi$date, climatology = TRUE
  )
}
